newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Defendants prepare to face death in Vietnam trial.
newsitem.headline: Defendants prepare to face death in Vietnam trial.

text.p: Leading defendants in Vietnam's dramatic drugs trial stared death in the face on Tuesday as judges met to consider their final verdicts in a case which has rocked the communist country's security establishment.
After a 10-day media frenzy surrounding the trial, state dailies carried sombre details of last statements made on Monday by the 22 accused shortly before court proceedings closed.

"There has been no injustice for me," said Vu Xuan Truong, the key defendant and former captain in the Interior Ministry's anti-crime unit. "I ask the judges for my execution to be carried out quickly."
Truong, who failed to make good on a promise to expose some "extremely important people", called for lenient sentencing for his wife and brother, also defendants.
But he said the judges should not hesitate to deal sternly with him and two other leading players.
"They were involved in crime with me," he said. "It was they who asked me to share the dirty money."
Final sentencing in the drugs scandal was expected late on Wednesday, but the tone and content of officially sanctioned media has left little room for doubt about verdicts.

"No matter where they might work... if they are involved in drugs trafficking or storage they must be punished, harshly punished," Communist Party chief Do Muoi was quoted as saying by the Ho Chi Minh City Police newspaper.
In a stark commentary on Monday, Voice of Vietnam radio also criticised the defence lawyers for defending their clients even after they had admitted guilt.
"Public opinion raises the question: whether in the current market economy lawyers work for defendants so that they are not objective...and continue to defend the accused."

Judges were expected to follow a prosecution recommendation calling for eight people to face death by firing squad. But court sources said leniency might be shown towards two women who had maintained their innocence throughout the proceedings.
Eight of the 14 others are expected to face life imprisonment, with the rest set for terms of up to 20 years.

The trial is the biggest drug scandal to surface in Vietnam. Half the 22 defendants are police and border security officials, most implicated by the confessions of a Laotian drug trafficker whose ultimate fate remains unknown.
Sieng Pheng broke down before he was about to be executed by firing squad two years ago and bargained for his life in return for providing information.
He then exposed a syndicate which is said to have shipped some 300 kilograms (660 pounds) of heroin to Vietnam and beyond from Asia's drug-producing Golden Triangle.

The trial is the latest in a series of high-profile cases which Vietnam's communist leaders say are aimed at demonstrating their determination to bolster the rule of law in a country where rules are routinely flouted, often through corruption.
At least nine people, including a Canadian and two Hong Kong men, have been sentenced to death so far this year for involvement in crimes involving corruption, fraud and drugs.
